name: Kaimati (Fried Dumplings)
instructions_text:
1. Put yeast in a small container.
2. Add 50ml of warmed water.
3. Add 4 tbsp. of sugar and allow to stand for 3 minutes.
4. Meanwhile, warm the rest of the water in a cooking pot.
5. Mix dry ingredients together; flour, cardamoms and vanilla
6. Add ¼ cup (50 g) of oil into the mixture and rub in until finely absorbed.
7. Add the yeast preparation to the flour mixture, adding the lukewarm water gradually while mixing to a semi-solid consistency.
8. Cover with a dry towel/ cloth and allow to stand for 4 minutes until the dough rises.
9. In a pan put the rest of the oil and heat for 7 minutes or until the oil bubbles when a pinch of dough is dropped in the oil.
10. Shape the dough into round balls and put into the hot oil, keep turning to cook evenly.
11. Deep fry for 3-4 minutes.
12. Remove from oil.
13. Mix the sugar, water and vanilla essence in a cooking pan.
14. Put on the heat for 5 minutes.
15. Stir to prevent sugar from sticking on the sides of the pan; the mixture should be sticky.
16. Add the fried dumplings to the sugar syrup and stir to coat them in the syrup while still on the heat.
17. Swirl until the syrup covers all the dumplings.
18. Serve as desired.
source: FAO/Government of Kenya. 2018. Kenyan Food Recipes

10. Set the dough aside for 10 minutes for sugar to dissolve. Cover with a cloth.

13. Divide the dough into small-medium size balls. Set them aside and cover with a dry cloth for 15 minutes.
14. When well raised, roll out each ball into flat discs and cut each into four triangle shaped portions.
15. Heat the remaining oil for 15 minutes to 173°C.
16. Fry the mahamri and turn after 40 seconds. The mahamri will turn golden brown when ready.
17. Remove the first batch of mahamri from oil and place onto paper towels to drain the oil.
18. Continue frying the rest in batches until all are done.
19. Serve as desired.

name: Groundnut Sauce
instructions_text:
1. Place a saucepan over fire and let it preheat.
2. Add the groundnuts, salt and ½ a cup of water or
3. Cook until the water evaporates as you stir gradually. When ready, the nuts produce a pop sound.
4. Once they pop, turn down the heat and continue stirring until the groundnuts are dry (about 13 minutes).
5. Remove from heat and allow it to cool down.
6. Using a blender, blend the nuts into a paste. A pestle and mortar can be used in the absence of a blender.
7. Put the groundnut paste into a bowl, add sour milk and stir into thick paste. Water or fresh milk can be used in place of the sour milk.
8. Once ready, put another pan on the heat, add the peanut paste and stir.
9. Stir until it is smooth but not too thick.
10. Serve hot with green leafy vegetables of your choice, fish, sweet potatoes, green bananas, ugali, etc.
